prerequisites: Basic engineering, biomedical-technological, and medical knowledge acquired during the Bachelor's degree in Biomedical Technology.

learning_outcomes.text: The student learns to think and act in an interdisciplinary context, specifically medical-technological, from an integrated and conceptual perspective.
The student learns to design in medical technology from three perspectives by executing a design project of a medical device or a medical-technological procedure and going through the entire process.

The student learns to design in medical technology from three perspectives by completing a one-week observation internship in a hospital, thereby experiencing the world of the technology user, specifically the doctor, from within.

The student learns to design in medical technology from three perspectives by participating in company and hospital visits, thus forming a good understanding of the state of contemporary medical technology in hospitals and medical-technological companies.
The student learns to think conceptually and abstractly and to design in an interdisciplinary context.
The student knows the course of a complete design process for a medical device or a medical-technological procedure.

The student approaches this project through a methodological and structured approach and learns, among other things, to take into account the specific boundary conditions imposed by the user (their function, specialty, characteristics of the patient group, uniqueness, etc.) and the medical context (standards, safety, etc.).

The student integrates basic medical and medical-technological knowledge with technological-scientific knowledge and builds upon the basic knowledge gained in previous Problem Solving and Design projects in the Bachelor's program.

Through observation of the actions of the medical or medical-technological specialist, through conversations and personal reflection, the student gets to know the medical environment for which the biomedical engineer designs technology, from within.
Thus, the student better understands how a biomedical engineer can best contribute, specifically which technology can be deployed and which design requirements best match hospital practice.
The student acquires additional insight into the contemporary state of affairs and evolution within the field of medical technology, and its use in hospitals and care institutions.
The student gains additional knowledge in contemporary design practice in the field of medical technology.

syllabus_topics: Design project in medical technology (students work in teams of two or three, choose a topic from a list provided by the didactic team, gathered from companies, clinical centers, research labs)
Detailed inventory of design requirements with special attention to the user context
Drawing up an agreement between client and student team
Setting up a requirement tree and a functional decomposition
Developing and, where necessary, evaluating a design
Hospital observation internship (one week on at least one department within a hospital like orthopedics, neonatology, cardiology, pneumology, radiology, neurology, pediatrics, clinical lab, etc.)
Structured conversation between the student and a medical or medical-technological specialist of the involved department
Observing the daily activities of medical or medical-technological specialists, especially the technology used by the medical specialist
Company and hospital visits (at least one visit to a medical-technological company and at least one visit to the technical services of a large hospital)

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of the design project (report, oral explanation, defense)
Evaluation of the hospital observation internship (written report, feedback from specialist)
Attendance and active participation in company and hospital visits

assessment_rules: The final result is a rounded, weighted average of the unrounded partial scores of the design project (75%) and the hospital observation internship (25%). Passing the design project is a prerequisite to pass the course. If a student achieves a result of 9/20 or less on the design project, the result for the course will be a weighted average of partial scores with a maximum of 9/20. Insufficient participation in one or more parts of this course (design project, hospital internship, company or hospital visit) leads to a 'NA' result for both the first and second examination opportunities. Students who do not pass get a second examination opportunity, for which a new assignment will be defined.
